blocks.text: Verses 14–21 belong to Isaiah 40–55’s announcement of comfort and return from Babylon. Their images of a path through the sea and of water in the wilderness present that return as a new homecoming shaped by creation and exodus imagery. This promise of return does not imply that the trauma of displacement or conflict after return simply disappeared.

The Great Isaiah Scroll is an almost complete witness to all sixty-six chapters of Isaiah. It broadly aligns with the Masoretic tradition while containing thousands of spelling and substantive differences; other Isaiah manuscripts and interpretive writings from Qumran also show that the book was actively transmitted and interpreted.
